newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM hopes for budget approval on Friday - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India PM hopes for budget approval on Friday - PTI.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whose minority coalition faces a vote of confidence on Friday, was quoted on Wednesday as saying he hoped parliament would pass the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on that day.

"I even now expect and I hope that all political parties will cooperate to pass the Finance Bill and the budget pending before parliament on April 11," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted him as telling reporters in New Delhi.
"Let us not make the poor suffer because of our political desires," Deve Gowda was quoted as saying.
The Congress party withrew its vital support for Deve Gowda's coalition earlier this month.
The budget, presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on February 28, proposed tax cuts that pleased industry.
But opposition parties have said the budget, originally scheduled to be taken up for discussion and voting after April 21, cannot be passed in a hurry without being debated by parliamentary panels.

The United Front says if its government falls, the budget cannot be passed. To prove its majority, the United Front has to work out a fresh accord with the Congress, or the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) must abstain or support the government.
Last year, the United Front and the Congress party had closed ranks to oust a 12-day old government led by the BJP after it emerged as the biggest group in parliament after general elections.
